definitions.explanation: a thin stick used by a conductor to direct an orchestra, choir, or other musical ensemble

examples.japanese: ⟦{指揮者|しきしゃ}→指揮者：06565_shikisha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{指揮棒|しきぼう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}った→振る：01983_furu⟧。
{指揮棒|しきぼう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{動|うご}き→動き：11926_ugoki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧⟦{演奏|えんそう}する→演奏する：20349_ensousuru⟧。
examples.english: Play in time with the movements of the baton.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{指揮棒|しきぼう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{軽|かる}くて→軽い：00785_karui⟧⟦バランス→バランス：03870_baransu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{良|よ}い→良い：02350_yoi⟧。
examples.english: This baton is light and well-balanced.

notes:
USAGE:
The baton (⟦タクト→タクト：23985_takuto⟧ from German Taktstock is also used) is typically 10-15 inches long. Some conductors prefer not to use a baton and conduct with their hands only.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {指揮棒|しきぼう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}る→振る：01983_furu⟧ (to conduct; literally "wave the baton")
- {指揮棒|しきぼう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{握|にぎ}る→握る：02383_nigiru⟧ (to hold the baton; take up conducting)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{指揮者|しきしゃ}→指揮者：06565_shikisha⟧ (conductor)
- ⟦{指揮|しき}→指揮：11102_shiki⟧ (conducting; direction)
- ⟦タクト→タクト：23985_takuto⟧ (takt - baton, from German)
